introduction: The history engine computes in TypeScript what the hub computed by running git: three-way merges, rebases, merge commits and the replay of recorded conflict resolutions. It has no routes; its callers are the rebuild and merge packages. Its correctness criterion is equality with the real git binary, proved over a generated corpus.

glossary.conflict identity: A stable value the engine computes from a conflict's content, used to recognise the same conflict when it arises again and to key its recorded resolution. It need not equal git's rerere hash.
glossary.differential suite: The test suite that runs each case of a generated corpus through the engine and through the real git binary and fails on any difference in tree, parents, commit order or conflicting paths.
glossary.history engine: The module that applies one branch to another and reports the result, reading and writing objects through the repository store and running no external program.
glossary.recorded resolution: A resolution stored against a conflict identity, applied automatically when that conflict arises again.
glossary.three-way merge: Combining two sides of a change against their common base, taking a one-sided change as it stands and reporting a conflict where both sides changed the same region differently.
glossary.unit of platform work: One invocation the platform will run to completion, bounded by its CPU, memory and wall-clock limits. Work too large for one continues in another.

requirements.title: Three-way merge
requirements.rationale: Every other operation here is built on it, so a flaw in the merge is a flaw in rebases, merge commits and replayed resolutions alike.

criteria.action: for a path changed on only one side of a base, take that side's content into the merged tree
criteria.contract: the merged tree's entry for that path equals the changed side's entry, in content and in mode

criteria.action: merge identical changes made on both sides without reporting a conflict
criteria.contract: the merged tree's entry equals the entry both sides produced, and the result carries no conflict

criteria.condition: both sides change the same region of one path differently
criteria.action: report a conflict naming that path and produce no merged tree
criteria.contract: the result is a conflict whose path list contains that path; no tree object is written

criteria.action: treat renames, mode changes, deletions, additions and binary files as the real git binary treats them
criteria.contract: for each of those shapes the merged tree, or the conflict, matches what git produces from the same base and sides

criteria.action: produce the same merged tree whichever of the two sides is given first, for any input that merges cleanly
criteria.contract: swapping the two sides yields an identical tree object id for every non-conflicting case

requirements.title: Rebase
requirements.rationale: This is how a patch stack is applied, so an extra, missing or reordered commit changes what a deployment ships.

criteria.condition: a branch is rebased onto a base
criteria.action: copy each of the branch's own commits onto the base, in their original order
criteria.contract: the resulting history holds one commit per original commit of the branch, in the same order, each with the base's history behind it

criteria.action: keep each copied commit's author and message, and give it a new committer and new parents
criteria.contract: for each copied commit the author and message equal the original's, the parent is the previously copied commit or the base, and the commit id differs from the original's

criteria.action: handle a commit whose changes are already present in the base as the real git binary handles it
criteria.contract: for a branch containing such a commit, the resulting history is identical to the one git produces from the same inputs

criteria.condition: copying one of the branch's commits conflicts
criteria.action: stop at that commit, report the conflicting paths, and apply none of the branch's later commits
criteria.contract: the result is a conflict naming the paths and the commit it stopped at; no later commit of the branch appears in any written object; the repository is unchanged

requirements.title: Merge strategy
requirements.rationale: The alternative rebuild strategy, chosen per workspace or per job, and wrong parentage here makes the integration branch's history unreadable.

criteria.condition: a branch is merged into a base
criteria.action: produce one merge commit whose parents are the base and the branch
criteria.contract: the resulting commit has exactly two parents, the first the base's head and the second the branch's head

criteria.action: set the merge commit's tree to the three-way merge of the base, the branch and their merge base
criteria.contract: the merge commit's tree object id equals the one git produces for the same merge

criteria.action: produce no commit and report the conflicting paths
criteria.contract: no commit or tree object is written; the result names every conflicting path

requirements.title: Conflicts
requirements.rationale: A conflict is reported to a user and recorded for replay, so its path list and its identity are both part of the contract.

criteria.action: report every path that conflicted and no path that merged cleanly
criteria.contract: the reported path set equals the set git reports for the same inputs

criteria.action: compute a conflict's identity from its content, so that the same conflict arising again yields the same identity
criteria.contract: two occurrences of the same conflict yield equal identities; two different conflicts yield different identities; the identity is unchanged across restarts

criteria.condition: an operation ends in a conflict
criteria.action: leave the repository exactly as it was before the operation began
criteria.contract: the ref list and every ref's target are unchanged, and no object written during the attempt is reachable from any ref

requirements.title: Recorded resolutions
requirements.rationale: Replaying a resolution is what makes a repeated rebuild of a long patch stack survivable; without it every rebuild stops at the same conflict.

criteria.action: record the resolution against that conflict's identity
criteria.contract: the resolution is afterwards listed for that identity with resolved true

criteria.guard: a resolution is recorded for that conflict's identity
criteria.action: apply the recorded resolution and continue the operation
criteria.contract: the operation completes without reporting that conflict, and its result equals the result of the same operation with the resolution applied by hand

criteria.action: keep a recorded resolution beyond the invocation and the process that recorded it
criteria.contract: a resolution recorded before a restart is applied to the same conflict after it

criteria.condition: the recorded resolutions of a repository are listed
criteria.action: report each with its identity, the path where it is known, when it was recorded, and whether a resolution is recorded or only the conflict has been seen
criteria.contract: every entry carries an identity and a recorded time; path is present where the engine knows it and absent otherwise; resolved is true only when a resolution will be replayed

criteria.condition: a resolution is forgotten by identity, or by path while that path is in conflict
criteria.action: remove it, so the conflict is reported again next time
criteria.contract: the entry is gone from the listing and the next occurrence of that conflict is reported rather than replayed; forgetting by a path that is not in conflict removes nothing and says so

requirements.title: Equivalence with the real git binary
requirements.rationale: This engine stands in for git; near-enough is a silently wrong history, and only a comparison against git can show the difference.

criteria.action: for any case the differential corpus holds, produce the history the real git binary produces from the same inputs with the same strategy
criteria.contract: the resulting tree object id, each commit's parent list and the order of the commits are identical to git's for every case

criteria.action: for any corpus case that conflicts, report the same conflicting paths the real git binary reports
criteria.contract: the two path sets are equal, and a case that conflicts for one and not the other is a failure

criteria.action: cover at least 200 generated histories spanning linear and branching history, renames, binary files, mode changes, empty commits, merge commits in the source, conflicting and clean patches, and a stack of at least 20 patches
criteria.contract: the corpus holds at least 200 cases and at least one of each named shape, and every case runs through both implementations

requirements.title: Size and progress
requirements.rationale: Worker CPU and memory bound the work, and an operation that stalls or is killed half way is worse than one that refuses.

criteria.action: apply a stack of at least 50 patches onto a repository of at most 500 MB of packed objects, with at most 1000 changed files and 10 MB of diff per patch
criteria.contract: the operation completes and its result matches git's for the same inputs

criteria.condition: an operation exceeds the stated patch count, repository size, changed-file count or diff size
criteria.action: fail with a reason naming the limit exceeded rather than stalling
criteria.contract: the failure names which limit was exceeded; the operation does not run past the platform's limits and is not killed

criteria.condition: an operation cannot finish within one unit of platform work
criteria.action: continue it in another and carry it to completion
criteria.contract: an operation spanning several units completes with the same result as one that fits in a single unit

criteria.condition: an operation fails or is abandoned part way
criteria.action: leave the repository as it was before it began
criteria.contract: the ref list and every ref's target are unchanged, and no partial result is reachable from any ref

requirements.title: The engine as a module
requirements.rationale: Two packages will drive it, and the deployment has no git binary to fall back on if it quietly depends on one.

criteria.action: read and write objects and refs only through the repository store interface
criteria.contract: the engine's operations succeed against both implementations of the repository store, with no direct use of either

criteria.action: run where no git binary is present
criteria.contract: every operation of the engine succeeds in an environment with no git executable on the path

execution_paths.title: A branch is rebased in a real repository and the result is readable

steps.action: asks the history engine to rebase a branch onto a base in a workspace's repository
reads the commits, trees and blobs it needs through the repository store
copies each of the branch's commits onto the base, three-way merging each change
stores the new objects and the updated ref
reads the new head and finds the expected commits, in order, with the base's history behind them

execution_paths.title: A conflict is resolved once and replayed after a restart

steps.action: applies a patch that conflicts and receives the conflicting paths and the conflict's identity
resolves the conflict and records the resolution against that identity
applies the same patch onto the same base again
recognises the conflict, applies the recorded resolution and completes without reporting a conflict

execution_paths.title: The generated corpus agrees with the real git binary

steps.action: generates a corpus of at least 200 histories covering the named shapes
runs each case and reports its resulting history or its conflicting paths
runs the same case on the same inputs
compares the tree, the parents, the commit order and the conflicting paths and fails on any difference
